says: The machine_path shape matches a slash, the word home and a slash anywhere in a line, so a repo-relative path through a folder named home, such as the home folder of law 5's saved home in fixtures/next/port-home, is read as a leak and blocks a push.
proof: leakgrep.sh --text on a file holding only the repo-relative path of brain.json in law 5's saved home (fixtures, next, port-home, home, brain.json, joined by slashes) exits 1 with 'leak machine_path at added line 1'. On T502 S1 a .gitignore line naming that folder was refused before its push and had to be written with a '*' in place of the folder's name. This row cannot quote the path, for the same reason.
cost: Any text that names a file of law 5's saved home, in a comment, a plan row or a pull request body, is refused, and each later slice that saves a new home meets it; the way round is to write the path another way, which hides the name a reader would search for.
